paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the percentage of matches between Large Language Model (LLM) judgments and human annotations across 300 samples. The horizontal axis represents different levels of cognitive states, including "Self-aware," "Rigorous," "Correct," "Matched," and "Not Matched," listed in alphabetical order. The vertical axis displays the percentage match, ranging from 0% to 100%, with a linear scale. The value axis is labeled "Matched / Not Matched" and consists of six blue bars, each representing a specific cognitive state. The bar for “Correct” reaches 99.00%, the “Not Matched” bar reaches 1.00%, and the “Matched” bar reaches 98.33%. The remaining bars for “Self-aware”, “Rigorous”, “Oriented”, and “Active” each have values around 97.33% and 97.00% respectively, with the “Oriented” bar reaching 2.67% and the “Active” bar reaching 3.00%. All bars are presented in a uniform height and are not explicitly emphasized or sorted.
